title: Replacing Wilbur Kirk; trying to recall the personnel
summary: He took Wilbur Kirk's drum chair; Dance and Clarke try unsuccessfully to remember a famous trumpeter named George and the pianist.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, whose place did you take on drums?
Oh, why, what did he do?
Well, he left to go, to come to New York or something like that.
Something big was happening for him.
I don't know what it was. I think he became -- he left to come to New York.
And that's why, Mary Lou got news about it and that's why we stopped. We were going straight to Kansas
And so she got news about this and so she said, 'Well, maybe we can drop Kenny off here.'
Well, they dropped me off there, and I joined the band. And I stayed I guess, oh, --
Well, who else was in that band?
I'm trying to think who was in that band.
Let me see, I don't know whether the bass player -- no, it wasn't Jimmy Blanton at that time.
No. No, it wasn't Jimmy, because when I met Jimmy it was way in 1940, about six or seven years after.
Let's see, I'm trying to think -- but I remember there was a tenor player I remember very well. Oh, wait a minute now. George -- he became a very famous trumpet player.
-- trumpet player. Was in this band.
: A first man or a third trumpet player?
No, he was sort of all around trumpet player, a good soloist --
: You're not talking about Harold Baker, are you?
No, I don't think Harold was in that band. They were all older musicians, much older.
: Oh, there was a good trumpet player that went with Teddy Wilson later.
It could have been a trombone player. Because I didn't get very close. They were very older fellows.
Well, Teddy had a brother, Gus, who played trombone.
: Yeah, that's right, he did didn't he.
And, oh, that trumpet player -- he came to New York. He became quite famous for awhile.
George. I can't think of his last name.
Well, listen, you will. You think it over. Tomorrow some of these names will come back to you.
I'll look through some of my papers and things and maybe I might find it.
Yeah. Well, it doesn't really matter, except that it's just interesting what you do remember, you know?
Who was on the piano? Was it a good piano player? You don't remember.
Oh, yeah, he was a good piano player, whoever he was. I remember now.
Because we had to play such difficult music.
So as far as I can remember they were all excellent musicians.
